why: The Outlet was founded to push the idea of a shared net of archives, agreed by the major newspapers of the day. It carries text only; photographs are not yet part of it.

bst.why: Founded in Ba Sing Se in 220 BG with the help of the Avatar Kyoshi. It has been the Earth Kingdom’s paper of record ever since.
bst.a: The Earth Kingdom’s paper of record, printed in Ba Sing Se. Formal, measured, and slow to print what it has not confirmed.
bst.std: Two named sources for any claim of fact about the state. Corrections run in the same column, in the same type.
rules: Every dispatch carries a dateline, a signature or desk credit, and the hour it was filed.
Casualty figures are printed only from a named authority, and marked as such.
Editorials are unsigned, and say so.

qr.why: Founded in 170 AG as a politics paper for the Qianchan Republic. Over the years it widened from politics to international news, and it later gave up print to become a strictly online paper.
qr.a: Voice of the federal republic of the south: industrial, numerate and proud of its tables.
qr.std: Every figure printed can be traced to a table the reader may ask to see. Reports are signed; letters are answered in the same page.
rules: Statistics run with their source and date.
Letters to the editor are answered in the next edition.
Reports are signed by the reporter, not the desk.

rd.why: Founded by press who had covered the war for Gaozu. They trained local staffers on the peninsula, and it made more sense to found a new paper for the new Republic than to carry an old one across the sea.
rd.a: Daily of the council republic that grew from the Fire Nation’s former colonies, written for readers born in four nations.
rd.std: Council sessions are reported from the verbatim record. Anyone named in a story is offered a right of reply in the same edition.
rules: Quotations come from the session record, not from memory.
Right of reply on every story that names a person.
Notices are printed for all four peoples of the republic.

cs.why: Founded in Caldera City not long after the bankruptcy of the Scire, the capital’s earlier paper, which it came to replace.
cs.a: The Empire’s capital paper, printed in Caldera City. Official statements run in full and are boxed and labelled as such.
cs.std: Communiqués are printed in full and marked as communiqués; the paper’s own reporting is never set in the same type. Diet proceedings are quoted from the transcript.
rules: Official statements are boxed and labelled.
Diet speeches are quoted from the transcript.
The paper’s reporting and the government’s are never set in the same type.

gaozu.why: Founded in Gaoling in 260 BG as the propaganda arm of the Beifong family. It is now the official newspaper of the government.
gaozu.a: A daily of Qianchan, printed in Gaoling and founded in AG 14. Orderly, dated twice over, and careful to keep praise out of its reporting.
gaozu.std: Every dispatch is dated by both calendars. Figures are printed with the office that supplied them.
rules: Every dispatch is dated by both calendars.
Figures are printed with the office that supplied them.
Praise and report are never set in the same column.

report.d: Straight news: inverted pyramid, dateline, two justified columns, end mark.
rules: Lede: who, what, when and where in one sentence of 35 words or fewer; the why and how come next.
Inverted pyramid: facts in descending order of importance, so the story can be cut from the bottom.
Attribute every claim of fact to a named source (“said”, not “claimed”); anonymous sources only with the editor’s consent.
Two independent sources for any claim about the state, casualties or a crime.
Opinion stays out of the news columns; analysis is labelled as analysis.
Quote exactly; never fix what is inside quotation marks.
Paragraphs of one to three sentences; spell out numbers below ten; write a.m. and p.m.
A correction runs on the same page, in the same type, as soon as an error is confirmed.

## Crosshead

wire.d: Teletype bulletin: one narrow monospaced column, END mark.
rules: Slug first: SLUG, priority, hour filed.
Priority: FLASH for a first alert of 25 words or fewer, BULLETIN for a major update, URGENT for a significant one, ADD for further text.
No adjectives and no analysis; only verified facts and the source.
Replace the whole item with a WRITETHRU when the facts change; never edit silently.
End with END; mark unfinished text MORE.

rules: Unsigned: it speaks for the paper as “we”.
One question, one argument, argued fully.
State the strongest opposing argument fairly, then answer it.

Keep it out of the news pages and label it as opinion.

agencies: Kyoshi Plate Syndicate | Earth Kingdom | AG 88 | A plate is a witness. | Plates are never retouched past dust and scratches. Each plate is filed with photographer, place and hour. On The Outlet only the caption line is carried; the plate follows by courier.
charter:
The Outlet is the international press collective of the four nations: a shared desk, wire and archive kept by the major newspapers, wire services and photo agencies of the Earth Kingdom, the Qianchan Republic, the United Republic of Nations and the Empire of Tajisaki. Members keep their own mastheads and their own editors. What they share is a dateline, a filing format and a code of practice.

Every story carries a dateline, a signature or a desk credit, and the hour it was filed. Corrections run on the same page in the same type. Official statements are labelled as official statements. Casualty figures are printed only with a named authority.

Photo-agency members file their pictures in their own archives. This site carries text only.
